title: The Passage of Cape Reckoning
premise: Paloma Pemberton, estranged from her archaeologist father and drifting through coastal odd jobs, is given a hand-drawn map by a dying prospector in exchange for a promise to deliver it somewhere safe. The map leads to a drowned temple off Cape Reckoning that her father has spent his life searching for, and Paloma must team up with a disgraced boat pilot named Idris Vale to reach it before the monsoon seals the coast. Racing a rival salvage crew backed by a corrupt port magistrate who wants the temple's artifacts for himself, Paloma discovers the site holds proof of her father's greatest theory — and his disappearance. In the climax she chooses love and belonging over the treasure's power, flooding the temple rather than surrendering it, and returns home not with riches but with the family she built on the water.
about_author: Emrys Vasquez is a former merchant marine who spent a decade sailing the monsoon coasts of Southeast Asia before turning to writing full-time. Known for salt-stained prose and morally tangled heroes, Vasquez lives aboard a restored ketch with an opinionated parrot named Cartographer.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Paloma Pemberton's POV. Working a salvage dock in Port Amara, Paloma measures her life in distance traveled since walking out on her father three years ago. A letter from him arrives unopened in her kit. Emotional beat: restless loneliness disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A feverish old prospector named Hollis collapses at her campfire and trades her a grease-stained map for a promise: carry it to the Cape, tell no one. He dies by dawn. Emotional beat: the weight of a promise made too easily.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Studying the map, she recognizes her father's handwriting in its margins — he annotated it years ago. The destination matches his life's obsession: a drowned temple beneath Cape Reckoning. Emotional beat: the past reaching out with cold fingers.

chapters.title: A Boat Called Mercy
chapters.summary: Idris Vale's POV. Disgraced pilot Idris, banned from legitimate charters after a scandal he won't explain, agrees to take a stranger up the coast for coin. He notices she's being watched. Emotional beat: a man buying back his honor one risky job at a time.

chapters.title: Departure at Slack Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They slip out of Port Amara ahead of a storm front, pursued briefly by men flying the magistrate's colors. Paloma lies to Idris about what the map is. Emotional beat: guilt as ballast.

chapters.title: The Wreck of Sable Key
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Sheltering at a wreck-strewn cay, they dive a half-sunken freighter for supplies and find evidence someone else is hunting the same waters. First real conversation between them. Emotional beat: wary respect kindling.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Men
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Salvage captain Oren Blackwood, working for Magistrate Corvane, boards them under pretense of inspection and searches for the map. Paloma hides it inside her father's letter. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into cunning.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Cape
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The Mercy takes hull damage in open water; they pump and patch through the night while the monsoon builds behind them. Idris reveals a fragment of his disgrace. Emotional beat: two broken people bailing together.

chapters.title: The Fisher Village of Low Anchor
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Repairs force a stop at a village where her father once worked; elders remember him fondly and speak of a 'second expedition' that never returned. Paloma learns he vanished near the Cape. Emotional beat: grief arriving years late.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Magistrate Corvane intercepts them personally, offering Idris reinstatement and pardon if he delivers Paloma and the map. Idris refuses — but Corvane lets them go, clearly tracking them. Emotional beat: temptation weighed and set down.

chapters.title: Halfway Truths
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Confronted about the lie, Paloma finally shows Idris the whole map and admits the missing man is her father. Idris confesses his scandal: he was blamed for a sinking caused by his employer's shortcuts. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt on honest wreckage.

chapters.title: The Storm Gate
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. To reach the Cape before the monsoon closes the strait, they must run a reef passage locals call the Storm Gate — a death run Idris alone knows. White-knuckle navigation through collapsing swells. Emotional beat: courage as a shared act.

chapters.title: Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They anchor in the Cape's shadowed cove and locate the temple entrance beneath a collapsed sea arch. Diving down, Paloma finds modern gear — recent visitors. Someone has been here within weeks. Emotional beat: dread beneath wonder.

chapters.title: The Drowned Temple
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inside the flooded halls, carvings confirm her father's theory: a civilization that measured wealth in what it gave away. She finds his journal wedged in a shrine — dated after his disappearance. He was alive here. Emotional beat: hope like a lungful of air.

chapters.title: Blackwood's Net
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Surfacing, they find the Mercy boarded and Oren Blackwood waiting, holding Idris's beloved boat hostage for the map and their silence. Corvane's ship anchors offshore. Emotional beat: everything they love suddenly leverage.

chapters.title: The Price of Power
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Brought before Corvane, Paloma witnesses his true aim: not scholarship but dominion — the temple's 'gift economy' relics repurposed as symbols to legitimize his rule. He offers her partnership, revealing her father refused the same offer. Emotional beat: seeing corruption wear a civilized face.

chapters.title: What Her Father Left Behind
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following clues in the journal, Paloma finds her father's hidden camp in the cliffs above the cove — and learns he died protecting the temple's location, leaving her a final message: some things must stay buried to stay sacred. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the dead.

chapters.title: The Choice Below
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Corvane forces a guided descent to loot the central vault. Paloma realizes the temple's flood-channels can be opened deliberately — drowning the vault and sealing the site forever, at the risk of everyone inside. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax. As Corvane's men breach the vault, Paloma opens the channels. Water thunders through the halls; Idris drags her out as the temple collapses inward. Corvane, refusing to abandon the treasure, is lost. Emotional beat: sacrifice crowned with terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Aftermath on Open Water
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Adrift in a damaged tender, survivors of both crews must cooperate or die; Blackwood, humbled, helps them reach shore. Corvane's regime begins to crack without his prize. Emotional beat: enemies softened by shared survival.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma delivers word of Hollis's map to the fisherfolk of Low Anchor, honoring the promise in spirit — the knowledge given to people who would guard it, not spend it. She reads her father's letter at last. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later, Paloma and Idris refit the Mercy and charter honest work along the coast, the sea finally feeling like home rather than escape. Paloma measures her life no longer in miles. Emotional beat: arrival — quiet, earned, and complete.
